newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy tries to pump life into Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy tries to pump life into Mideast peace.

text.p: U.S President Bill Clinton's Middle East peace envoy said on Sunday he was meeting Israeli and Palestinian leaders in hopes of resuscitating talks fading over Hebron and Jewish settlements.

"The important thing that I am trying to do is to re-energise the peace process and then be in a position to go back in a couple of days to report back to the president," envoy Dennis Ross told reporters.

Arriving late on Saturday, Ross went straight into meetings with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem and with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in self-ruled Gaza. His last mediation effort collapsed in October.

Arafat, who earlier cast doubts on Ross's objectivity, said after meeting the U.S. envoy for 2-1/2 hours early on Sunday: "It was very constructive and fruitful and an important meeting. We discussed how to push the peace process forward in all means."
Arafat's spokesman Nabil Abu Rdainah said Ross brought several ideas aimed at closing a deal on Hebron.
Israelis and Palestinians accuse each other of foot-dragging in talks on the West Bank town, 80 percent of which was due to have been handed over to Arafat's Palestinian Authority months ago.

Negotiators for both sides met again on Sunday, Palestinian officials said. Netanyahu wants a deal signed in 1995 changed to protect some 400 militant Jewish settlers in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs.

Abu Rdainah said Ross's ideas focused on four main points: Israel's demand to be able to pursue suspects in Palestinian areas, reopening Martyrs Street in the heart of town that was closed to Palestinians, arming Palestinian police as provided in the original accord and joint Israeli-PLO patrols.

"I hope the Palestinian Authority will understand there's no point in foot-dragging any longer," Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said before meeting Ross on Sunday. Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai also met the U.S. envoy.
Underscoring tensions in Hebron, a firebomb landed beside a Jewish settler home, igniting but causing no injuries. The army imposed a curfew while searching for the attackers.
In the West Bank near Bethlehem, an Israeli soldiers' hitchhiking post was damaged in an explosion apparently caused by Palestinian guerrillas but no one was injured, the army said.

U.S. Ambassador Martin Indyk said last week mistrust, rather than issues, was holding up a Hebron deal. The PLO wants assurances Netanyahu will carry out other deals signed by Israel's previous centre-left government once the deal on Hebron is carried out.

Palestinians were encouraged when Clinton criticised Israel's expansion of Jewish settlements in the West Bank last week but Secretary of State Warren Christopher's subsequent comment that Palestinians had to make gestures on Hebron irked PLO leaders.
"The most important thing is that Mr Ross has to be an accurate mediator, and not to be biased on the side of Israel," Arafat said on Friday.

Clinton last sent Ross after clashes in September in the West Bank and Gaza claimed the lives of 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis. He left after three weeks of mediation over Hebron saying the sides had narrowed the gaps but failed to reach a deal.
